questions.question: Two straight lines cross and one angle is 70 degrees. Give the other three angles with reasons.
questions.expected_answer: The angle vertically opposite the 70 is 70 degrees, vertically opposite angles. Each of the other two is 180 minus 70, which is 110 degrees, angles on a straight line. The four add to 360.

questions.question: A transversal makes 65 degrees with one of two parallel lines. State the corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles at the other line.
questions.expected_answer: Corresponding angle 65 degrees, equal; alternate angle 65 degrees, equal; co-interior angle 180 minus 65, which is 115 degrees, supplementary. Each reason must name the parallel lines.

questions.question: Why must a reason such as alternate angles name the parallel lines?
questions.expected_answer: Because the relationship holds only when the two lines crossed by the transversal are parallel. Without parallel lines, alternate angles are not equal, so naming the lines states the condition that makes the reason valid.
